recent_posts.title: Honest review of three community-built React Native apps
recent_posts.summary: A video review of three React Native apps built by community members, covering Inkigo (AI tattoo preview app), Momentos (location-based memory app), and Word Rain (a typing game). Each app is evaluated for UI/UX quality, onboarding flow, use of animations and haptics, AI integration, and monetization strategy. Key feedback includes praise for Inkigo's polished onboarding and subtle AI usage, criticism of Momentos' confusing save/action UI, and appreciation for Word Rain's Skia-powered performance with suggestions for UI simplification and a leaderboard feature.

recent_posts.title: The Mental Challenge of building a Game alone
I Thought I Broke My App… I Didn’t.  #mobileappdevelopment
What running a solo mobile game actually looks like after launch
recent_posts.summary: A solo developer shares the reality of running a mobile game (Tiny Harvest) after launch. While coding is only about 20% of the weekly workload, the rest involves bug triage, game balancing, customer support, marketing, App Store optimization, and TikTok outreach. Three major challenges are highlighted: the ongoing technical grind (endless bugs, balancing issues, players breaking things), the invisible full-time job of wearing 5-10 hats simultaneously, and the mental toll of sole ownership — including monetization guilt, slow days, and taking every criticism personally. A near-fatal moment came during a full game engine rewrite that took three stressful days with heavy AI assistance. Despite the hardships, the rewards of player engagement, creative fulfillment, and skill growth make it worthwhile.

recent_posts.title: Handling contradictory user feedback as an indie app developer
recent_posts.summary: A mobile game developer shares a personal experience of receiving contradictory feedback on the same day — a one-star review criticizing AI use and a glowing email praising the game's UI. The takeaway is that creators should expect polarized opinions, read between the lines, and not let negative feedback derail them, since people come from different backgrounds and will always perceive work differently.

recent_posts.title: $3,000 March Indie Game Revenue from IAP
recent_posts.summary: An indie developer shares five lessons from earning $3,000 in March from their mobile game Tiny Harvest via in-app purchases. Key takeaways include: an App Store feature drove a significant but short-lived download spike, IAP remains an effective monetization strategy, App Store Optimization (ASO) is critical with focus on screenshots, preview videos, and keywords, onboarding improvements dramatically reduced churn, and revenue volatility is normal so persistence is essential.

recent_posts.title: 7 lessons from shipping an indie mobile game with React Native and AI
recent_posts.summary: A solo developer shares 7 lessons from building Tiny Harvest, an indie mobile game built with React Native that earned $2,500. Key takeaways include: AI accelerates development but also amplifies mistakes and doesn't replace thinking; game design complexity (balancing, item dependencies) is brutally hard; early technical decisions compound over time (e.g., choosing offline-first with SQLite caused pain when adding online features); community feedback is invaluable but emotionally challenging; monetization signals product-market fit; Reddit outperformed Apple Ads and TikTok for user acquisition; and React Native with Expo/EAS proved reliable for cross-platform mobile game development.

recent_posts.title: App store listing tweaks that boosted game downloads from 30 to 200 per day
recent_posts.summary: A mobile game developer shares how small App Store listing changes boosted daily downloads from ~30 to 200+. The key changes were: updating keywords, app title, and subtitle to better target the RPG community; optimizing the first two screenshots to be more on-brand and value-focused; and updating the preview video poster image. The core lesson is that your app store page must clearly communicate what your app is about to the right audience, since people download the idea of your app, not the app itself.

recent_posts.title: How redesigning onboarding cut early player drop-off in half
recent_posts.summary: A mobile game developer shares how they lost over 50% of players in the first 10 minutes due to poor onboarding. The fix involved replacing a passive menu explanation with a guided, step-by-step onboarding flow that highlights exactly where to tap, delivers early wins, and sets consecutive goals between levels 5 and 10. The result was improved player retention and better progression through game mechanics. Key takeaway: if users don't understand your app within the first 60 seconds, they'll leave — fix onboarding before adding new features.
